# Results — Study 639 (Gasoline RVP Seasonality)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **every
spring, US gasoline specs switch to the expensive summer blend on a DATED regulatory calendar**
(40 CFR 1090.215: summer-RVP fuel at refineries/terminals by **May 1**, winter blend legal again
after **September 15**), so the gasoline-minus-crude spread should run up in **Feb–Apr** and give
it back in **Sep** — a seasonal with an actual law behind it. Measured on the monthly log-excess
of the RBOB front-month chain (`RB=F`) over the WTI front-month chain (`CL=F`), per-year panel
across ~21 years, with `UGA` (a real front-month holder) as the investable / curve test. Offline
& deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `ef905dc22f3c`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes: `RB=F` (RBOB front-month chain), `CL=F` (WTI front-month chain, the control leg), `UGA` (United States Gasoline Fund ETF, total-return), `^IRX` (13-week T-bill, for the excess-vs-cash race) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (**5,412** daily rows; **257** monthly excess observations 2005-02 → 2026-06; UGA from 2008-02) |
| Signal | monthly log-excess `log(1+r_RB) − log(1+r_CL)` — a dollar-neutral, monthly-rebalanced gasoline-over-crude spread; run-up window = **Feb–Apr**, switch-back = **Sep** |
| Execution / costs | the calendar is a **statute known years in advance**; entries use the **prior month-end close** (strictly earlier information — the one-lag rule is satisfied with room to spare); long-only UGA overlay charged **5/10/20 bps one-way × NAV**, one round trip per year, plus a net-of-T-bill excess-vs-cash race; no shorts in the retail vehicle (the UGA−CL crack is measured as a monthly-rebalanced excess, futures short pays no borrow) |

> **The splice caveat (named up front).** Yahoo's `RB=F`/`CL=F` are **spliced front-month
> chains**: at each roll the series jumps to the next contract's price — a jump **no holder
> earns**. The spliced series therefore tracks the **spot price level** seasonal, roll markup
> included. That is exactly the object the RVP *claim* is about (pump/spot gasoline vs crude), so
> the Signal axis reads the splice **labelled as a spot proxy** — and the Tradability and third
> axes read `UGA`, the real holder who pays every roll. No survivorship: the panel is two
> futures chains and one still-listed ETF, not a survivor basket of names.

## Signal — the Feb–Apr run-up on the gasoline-minus-crude spread (spot proxy)

Per-year panel: each year contributes its Feb–Apr mean monthly excess and its rest-of-year mean
monthly excess; the primary test is a **Welch t across the ~21 yearly pairs**.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| Feb–Apr mean monthly excess | **+3.77%/mo** |
| rest-of-year mean monthly excess | −1.22%/mo |
| gap (window − rest) | **+4.98%/mo** · **Welch *t* (years) = +6.20** (n = 21) |
| per-year cumulative window excess | **+11.30%** · one-sample *t* = **+5.10** · positive **90.5%** of years |
| pooled-months Welch *t* | +4.23 (66 window months vs 191 rest) |

The seasonal is unmistakable at the price level: gasoline out-runs crude by **+11.3% every
Feb–Apr window on average**, positive in 19 of 21 years, Welch *t* across years **6.20**.

## Per-calendar-month excess (Bonferroni ×12 bar ≈ |t| ≥ 3.0)

| month | mean %/mo | *t* | n | | month | mean %/mo | *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Jan | +0.57 | +0.31 | 21 | | Jul | +0.71 | +0.59 | 21 |
| Feb | +1.34 | +0.88 | 22 | | Aug | −0.50 | −0.19 | 21 |
| **Mar** | **+8.62** | **+5.34** ✅ | 22 | | **Sep** | **−6.88** | **−3.12** ✅ | 21 |
| Apr | +1.72 | +0.95 | 22 | | Oct | −2.82 | −1.67 | 21 |
| May | −0.39 | −0.26 | 22 | | Nov | +0.10 | +0.09 | 21 |
| Jun | −1.54 | −1.21 | 22 | | Dec | +0.79 | +0.73 | 21 |

Only two months clear the 12-test Bonferroni bar — and they are **exactly the two the statute
names**: **March** (the run-up into the May-1 refinery/terminal deadline, +8.62%/mo, *t* = 5.34)
and **September** (the switch-back after Sep 15, −6.88%/mo, *t* = −3.12, negative in 85.7% of
years). The calendar in the data matches the calendar in the Federal Register.

*Bar detail (referee note): the exact two-sided Bonferroni-×12 critical value at these df is
t ≈ 3.22. March clears it outright either way; September (|t| = 3.12) clears the **one-sided**
directional bar (t ≈ 2.93) — the sign is pre-registered by the statute — but sits just under the
exact two-sided value. The Signal stamp does not lean on this table: it is carried by the
Feb–Apr Welch t = 6.20 and both halves clearing t ≥ 2 alone.*

## Robustness — window variants + halves

| window | cum %/window | one-sample *t* | Welch *t* (years) | hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Mar only | +8.78 | +5.22 | +5.61 | 90% |
| Mar–Apr | +10.14 | +6.00 | +6.80 | 90% |
| **Feb–Apr (headline)** | **+11.30** | **+5.10** | **+6.20** | **90%** |
| Feb–May | +10.91 | +5.22 | +6.38 | 90% |

| half | mean window cum | *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005–2015 | +9.60% | +2.77 | 11 |
| 2016–2025 | +13.18% | +4.81 | 10 |

Every window variant clears *t* ≥ 5; **both halves clear *t* ≥ 2 independently**. Not a
sub-period artefact, not a window-choice artefact.

## Third axis — does the futures curve already price it?

Per-year, same window: cumulative log return of **UGA** (a real front-month holder who pays
every roll) minus the **spliced** `RB=F` chain (which banks each roll jump for free). Paired
one-sample *t* on the gap.

| window | spliced chain | holder (UGA) | roll gap | paired *t* | gap < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Feb–Apr** | **+16.08%** | +5.68% | **−10.40%/window** | **−8.06** | **18/18 years** |
| Sep | −7.96% | −1.58% | **+6.38%/month** | +4.95 | 1/18 years |

The curve prices the statute almost perfectly: of the +16.1% the spliced chain gains each spring
window (2009–2026 common sample), **−10.4 points are the roll markup** — paid by anyone actually
holding, negative in **every single one of 18 years**. And the mirror image holds in September:
the holder is *protected* on the way down (+6.4%/month gap) because the curve already discounts
the switch-back. The seasonal lives in the **curve**, not in the holder's P&L. *(The gap also
contains UGA's ~0.75%/yr expense ratio and its T-bill collateral interest — second-order beside
a 10-point window gap.)* **CONFIRMED.**

## Tradability — what a real holder can actually capture

**The investable crack** (long UGA / short CL, monthly rebalanced, 2009–2026):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| Feb–Apr window mean monthly excess | −0.06%/mo (rest: +0.61%/mo) |
| per-year cumulative window excess | **−0.18%** · one-sample *t* = **−0.07** · positive 47.1% of years (n = 17) |
| Welch *t* (years) | −0.74 |
| Sep excess | −0.02%/mo · *t* = −0.01 (n = 18) |

**The long-only UGA overlay** (hold Feb–Apr only, one round trip/yr):

| one-way cost | gross %/window | net %/window | *t* (net) | hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | +9.45 | +9.35 | +1.48 | 72.2% |
| 10 bps | +9.45 | +9.25 | +1.46 | 72.2% |
| 20 bps | +9.45 | +9.05 | +1.43 | 72.2% |
| 10 bps **+ window T-bill** (excess-vs-cash) | | **+8.91** | **+1.41** | 72.2% |

The tradable residue is a **coin flip**: the dollar-neutral investable crack earns **−0.18% per
window at *t* = −0.07** — the roll ate 100% of the seasonal, with change. The long-only UGA
spring window is big on average (+9.5%) but it is mostly **unhedged energy beta** with two
2008/2020-sized wrecks in the panel — *t* = 1.4 net of costs and cash, below the bar at every
cost level. Nothing here survives as an edge. **MIRAGE.**

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful *(never cited as evidence)*

Deterministic monthly world with a planted Feb–Apr seasonal (`amp`) mirrored in Sep, and a
planted curve-pricing drag on the holder (`roll_drag`). Each cell = mean *t* over **20 seeds**.

| world | Welch *t* (years) | window cum | Sep *t* | roll gap · *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (amp = 0, drag = 0) | −0.22 | −0.24% | +0.16 | +0.03% · +0.16 |
| planted (amp = 3%/mo, drag = 2%/mo) | **+4.61** | +8.76% | −2.76 | −5.97% · **−42.35** |

The null stays quiet on every detector; the planted world lights all of them up. The detectors
measure what they claim to measure.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The RVP-calendar seasonal on the gasoline-minus-crude spread is on the
  tape at the price level: Feb–Apr window **+11.30%/window** (Welch *t* across 21 years =
  **+6.20**, one-sample *t* = +5.10, 90.5% hit), and the only two Bonferroni-surviving calendar
  months are **exactly the two the statute names** — March (+8.62%/mo, *t* = +5.34) and
  September (−6.88%/mo, *t* = −3.12). Both halves independently significant. Measured on the
  spliced front-month chain, **labelled a spot-price proxy** (the splice caveat is named).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The curve already carries the law: a real front-month holder pays
  the seasonal back at every roll (**−10.4%/window**, paired *t* = **−8.06**, negative 18/18
  years). The investable crack (UGA−CL) earns **−0.18%/window at *t* = −0.07**; the long-only
  UGA window is sub-2 (*t* = 1.4) unhedged energy beta. Costs barely matter — there is nothing
  for them to eat.
- **"Does the futures curve already price it?" — CONFIRMED.** −10.4%/window roll gap in the
  run-up (paired *t* = −8.06, 18/18 years) and the mirror-image **+6.38%** giveback in
  September (*t* = +4.95). The RVP calendar is real, dated, and **fully priced** — the textbook
  case of a seasonal you can see but not buy.
